newsitem.title: USA: U.S. farm trade surplus $2.090 billion in November.
newsitem.headline: U.S. farm trade surplus $2.090 billion in November.

text.p: The U.S. trade surplus in agricultural commodities was $2.090 billion in November, up from a revised $1.481 billion in October, the Commerce Department said Friday.

In its monthly trade report, Commerce pegged farm exports at $5.045 billion in November, up from a revised $4.501 billion in October. Imports were $2.955 billion, compared with $3.020 billion the previous month.
The cumulative surplus in farm trade was $18.724 billion in the January to November period, compared with $15.514 billion in the same period last year.

In November, U.S. corn and soybean exports zoomed, with corn reaching $889 million, up $264 million, and soybeans $872 million, up $307 million. Wheat exports, at $372 million, were down $121 million, while exports of meat rose $13 million to $607 million.

Imports of most products fell slightly. Sugar was down $31 million to $42 million in November. Green coffee rose by $31 million to $201 million and frozen fruit juices gained $18 million to total $324 million.
The total for the single largest import category, fish and shellfish, was $605 million in November, down $1 million from October.
